transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled 45)
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Gabe (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood SA), Evan (NebulaSail Head of Platform), Marta (NebulaSail Infra), Samir (CTO), Jules (SecOps)

Summary:
Quick partner intro / discovery to scope a pilot for NebulaSail's cloud GPU offering to integrate Redwood inference as an option for their managed instances. Focus: VPC onboarding, keys/KMS, pricing split, routing/fallback for cost vs latency, and a small benchmark pilot.

Topics (auto): onboarding model, VPC / private control plane, SOC2 & KMS, dedicated vs hosted routing, pilot sizing, bench plan, integration owners

Action items (captured): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — really appreciate you making time. Quick round robin, then we'll jump into what NebulaSail is thinking and where Redwood might fit.
[00:22] Evan: Hi, Evan here — I'll give a 2-min look. We're a managed cloud provider focused on edge-friendly GPU instances, um, we want to offer inference-as-a-service through partners, not build everything ourselves.
[00:38] Marta: Marta — day-to-day on infra, we run k8s clusters in multiple clouds and our customers want predictable latency and cost.
[00:46] Priya: Awesome, makes sense. Gabe, you want to frame technical fit?
[00:50] Gabe: Yeah, quick sketch. Redwood runs a runtime that supports batching, kv-cache and quantized kernels; we can operate via hosted API for quick go-live, or dedicate capacity we co-manage on your GPU pools. For NebulaSail, two obvious patterns: 1) call Redwood hosted endpoints from your control plane, or 2) deploy Redwood Private in your VPC/tenant and we provide a private control plane and images.
[01:15] Samir: Quick question — if we go private, where do the keys live? We need HSM/KMS integration, and our customers require BYOK sometimes.
[01:24] Alex: Good point. We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK), and for on-prem or airgapped we can do customer-managed HSM. There's an audit log pipeline too.
[01:34] Jules: Are the audit logs searchable? We need 365-day retention for some customers.
[01:39] Gabe: Yes, logs are plumbed to your SIEM via S3 or direct syslog, retention configurable as an add-on. There may be egress costs if you pull big token traces.
[01:48] Evan: Sounds promising. Operationally we worry about two things: 1) cost attribution when partners spin up GPUs, and 2) graceful degradation — if the dedicated pool is busy, can Redwood route to cheaper models or other regions?
[02:05] Priya: Yup, we have smart routing and fallback policies — you can route by latency or cost and have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model or hosted fallback. You'll keep deterministic routing if you pin versions.
[02:18] Marta: Ok, so for billing, can we meter per-token and then charge customers? Or do we treat Redwood as a capacity contract?
[02:27] Gabe: Both options. For Marketplace / reseller flows, many partners choose per-token billing to end-customer and commit to a reserved capacity with Redwood to get price breaks. There's also a dedicated reserved capacity contract where you commit monthly and redistribute capacity inside your infra.
[02:45] Samir: We need examples — if a customer needs 200 qps at 512 tokens average, what GPU footprint is that?
[02:53] Gabe: We'll run benchmark templates. For a 512-token average, depending on the model family and quantization, it's around X-XS to 2 GPUs per 100 qps on A100-like hardware — but we'll run an actual sim. I'll send a short pilot sizing spreadsheet.
[03:09] Evan: Please call out latency SLOs. Our customers require p95 < 200ms for small chat style models.
[03:16] Gabe: We can target that with optimized kernels and smaller sequence lengths. For longer context models p95 goes up. We'll include p50/p95/p99 in the bench doc.
[03:24] Jules: Security folks will want to know how RBAC and tenant isolation works. Do you support per-tenant keys and per-tenant logs?
[03:32] Alex: Yes, multi-tenant isolation with namespaces and network policies. For Private deployments we recommend VPC/VPN segmentation and per-tenant KMS policies.
[03:40] Marta: Any special network setup? We run in multiple regions and prefer not to peer all VPCs.
[03:46] Priya: Many partners use a transit VPC pattern or colocated control plane with regional egress. We can also run sidecars so inference traffic stays intra-region. If you want full private plane, we can ship images you run in your cluster.
[03:59] Evan: If we run Redwood images in our infra, who manages upgrades?
[04:04] Alex: We handle control plane upgrades; for private deployments we can either push managed upgrades or let your infra team approve and apply images. Canary rollouts and automatic rollback are supported.
[04:15] Samir: We may need an on-prem airgapped option for certain customers. Is that supported?
[04:20] Gabe: Yep, we support airgapped bundles with offline package delivery and a customer-managed control plane. Key caveat: no hosted analytics unless you configure secure telemetry bridges.
[04:31] Marta: Ok — what about model licensing? Some customers want open models, some want provider-licensed ones.
[04:38] Priya: We have an open model catalog and verified performance profiles; licensed models can be integrated but require separate agreements. We'll surface per-model licensing notes.
[04:48] Jules: Have you done partner pilots like this before? Any references?
[04:51] Priya: Yes — we've run pilots with a couple of edge providers. I'll include two anonymized case studies and a reference contact.
[05:00] Evan: Good. Two other things: 1) can you support per-route token capping and throttles? 2) what telemetry hooks do you expose for tracing requests into our observability stack?
[05:10] Gabe: Per-route rate limits and token caps are configurable. For tracing, we emit request IDs and hooks for OpenTelemetry; you can ingest traces into your backend. We also provide dashboards surfaced in Redwood Console — per-token cost, per-model latency, and rollout traces.
[05:26] Marta: On the console, can we federate SSO to our IdP?
[05:30] Alex: SSO via SAML / OIDC is supported, RBAC through SCIM is possible. We'll share the SSO integration guide.
[05:37] Samir: What about network latency penalties? If we route to hosted fallback in us-east from eu-west, that's a problem for latency-sensitive customers.
[05:44] Gabe: Agreed. Routing policies can be region-aware; you can prefer local dedicated capacity then fallback to local hosted variants, and only cross-region as a last resort.
[05:54] Evan: On commercial, we need to see an example reseller pricing split and what reserved capacity discounts look like.
[06:01] Priya: We'll send an example. Typical splits are % reseller margin on top of per-token cost or a flat margin on committed capacity — we'll include both.
[06:12] Jules: Compliance: do you maintain SOC2 Type II?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 in process for some components. Will share certs.
[06:21] Marta: Great. I want to flag an internal constraint: we cannot store customer PII in third-party hosted logs. So if we use hosted fallback there must be redaction or not send transcripts.
[06:31] Gabe: We have redaction rules and can disable transcript shipping — tokens can be masked before logging. We'll call out data retention controls in the security packet.
[06:40] Evan: What's the fastest path to test this?
[06:43] Priya: Pilot: 4-week pilot, you provide a day-1 smoke test with 2 test customers generating 1k - 5k calls per day. Redwood provisions a dedicated pool or we use hosted depending on your preference. We run a bench and deliver a report.
[06:56] Samir: Sounds good. Who owns the bench plan?
[06:58] Gabe: Redwood will own the bench plan but need your instance inventory and an access window to run tests. We'll also provide a script so you can run locally.
[07:10] Evan: Ok, send the bench and the pilot sheet.
[07:12] Priya: Will do. Any other concerns?
[07:15] Jules: If we sign a reserved contract, what's the minimum term?
[07:19] Priya: Usually monthly with 3-month commit minimum for channel pricing; enterprise deals can adjust. We'll be explicit in the contract template.
[07:28] Marta: For metrics, we need cost per inference broken down by token and GPU hours — can your console export that?
[07:34] Alex: Yes, per-token + per-model + host-level cost breakdowns; exports to CSV/BigQuery.
[07:40] Evan: Great. I'm logging this on our side. Priya, can you send the SOC2 and the pilot pricing today or tomorrow?
[07:47] Priya: I'll send SOC2 and pilot pricing by EOD tomorrow. Gabe will share bench plan early next week.
[07:53] Samir: Alright, thanks all.
[07:55] Priya: Thanks, everyone — we'll recap next steps in the follow-up.

(End of recording)
